00144| | [`robots`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/robots#generate-a-robots-file)                  | `.js` `.ts` | Generated Robots file |
00145| 
00146| </AppOnly>
00147| 
00148| <PagesOnly>
00149| 
00150| ### File conventions
00151| 
00152| |                                                                                                             |                     |                   |
00153| | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------- |
00154| | [`_app`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/custom-app)                                          | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Custom App        |
00155| | [`_document`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/custom-document)                                | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Custom Document   |
00156| | [`_error`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/custom-error#more-advanced-error-page-customizing) | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Custom Error Page |
00157| | [`404`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/custom-error#404-page)                                | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | 404 Error Page    |
00158| | [`500`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/custom-error#500-page)                                | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | 500 Error Page    |
00159| 
00160| ### Routes
00161| 
00162| |                                                                                                |                     |             |
00163| | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------- |
00164| | **Folder convention**                                                                          |                     |             |
00165| | [`index`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts#index-routes)        | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Home page   |
00166| | [`folder/index`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts#index-routes) | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Nested page |
00167| | **File convention**                                                                            |                     |             |
00168| | [`index`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts#index-routes)        | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Home page   |
00169| | [`file`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts)                      | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Nested page |
00170| 
00171| ### Dynamic routes
00172| 
00173| |                                                                                                                   |                     |                                  |
00174| | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------- |
00175| | **Folder convention**                                                                                             |                     |                                  |
00176| | [`[folder]/index`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/dynamic-routes)                                  | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Dynamic route segment            |
00177| | [`[...folder]/index`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)            | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Catch-all route segment          |
00178| | [`[[...folder]]/index`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/dynamic-routes#optional-catch-all-segments) | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Optional catch-all route segment |
00179| | **File convention**                                                                                               |                     |                                  |
00180| | [`[file]`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/dynamic-routes)                                          | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Dynamic route segment            |
00181| | [`[...file]`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)                    | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Catch-all route segment          |
00182| | [`[[...file]]`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/dynamic-routes#optional-catch-all-segments)         | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Optional catch-all route segment |
00183| 
00184| </PagesOnly>
00185| 
00186| <AppOnly>
00187| 
00188| ## Organizing your project
00189| 
00190| Next.js is **unopinionated** about how you organize and colocate your project files. But it does provide several features to help you organize your project.
00191| 
00192| ### Component hierarchy
00193| 
00194| The components defined in special files are rendered in a specific hierarchy:
00195| 
00196| - `layout.js`
00197| - `template.js`
00198| - `error.js` (React error boundary)
00199| - `loading.js` (React suspense boundary)
00200| - `not-found.js` (React error boundary for "not found" UI)
00201| - `page.js` or nested `layout.js`
00202| 
00203| <Image
00204|   alt="Component Hierarchy for File Conventions"
00205|   srcLight="/docs/light/file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00206|   srcDark="/docs/dark/file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00207|   width="1600"
00208|   height="643"
00209| />
00210| 
00211| The components are rendered recursively in nested routes, meaning the components of a route segment will be nested **inside** the components of its parent segment.
00212| 
00213| <Image
00214|   alt="Nested File Conventions Component Hierarchy"
00215|   srcLight="/docs/light/nested-file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00216|   srcDark="/docs/dark/nested-file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00217|   width="1600"
00218|   height="863"
00219| />
00220| 
00221| ### Colocation
00222| 
00223| In the `app` directory, nested folders define route structure. Each folder represents a route segment that is mapped to a corresponding segment in a URL path.
00224| 
00225| However, even though route structure is defined through folders, a route is **not publicly accessible** until a `page.js` or `route.js` file is added to a route segment.
00226| 
00227| <Image
00228|   alt="A diagram showing how a route is not publicly accessible until a page.js or route.js file is added to a route segment."
00229|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-not-routable.png"
00230|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-not-routable.png"
00231|   width="1600"
00232|   height="444"
00233| />
00234| 
00235| And, even when a route is made publicly accessible, only the **content returned** by `page.js` or `route.js` is sent to the client.
00236| 
00237| <Image
00238|   alt="A diagram showing how page.js and route.js files make routes publicly accessible."
00239|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-routable.png"
00240|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-routable.png"
00241|   width="1600"
00242|   height="687"
00243| />
00244| 
00245| This means that **project files** can be **safely colocated** inside route segments in the `app` directory without accidentally being routable.
00246| 
00247| <Image
00248|   alt="A diagram showing colocated project files are not routable even when a segment contains a page.js or route.js file."
00249|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-colocation.png"
00250|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-colocation.png"
00251|   width="1600"
00252|   height="1011"
00253| />
00254| 
00255| > **Good to know**: While you **can** colocate your project files in `app` you don't **have** to. If you prefer, you can [keep them outside the `app` directory](#store-project-files-outside-of-app).
00256| 
00257| ### Private folders
00258| 
00259| Private folders can be created by prefixing a folder with an underscore: `_folderName`
00260| 
00261| This indicates the folder is a private implementation detail and should not be considered by the routing system, thereby **opting the folder and all its subfolders** out of routing.
00262| 
00263| <Image
00264|   alt="An example folder structure using private folders"
00265|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-private-folders.png"
00266|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-private-folders.png"
00267|   width="1600"
00268|   height="849"
00269| />
00270| 
00271| Since files in the `app` directory can be [safely colocated by default](#colocation), private folders are not required for colocation. However, they can be useful for:
00272| 
00273| - Separating UI logic from routing logic.
00274| - Consistently organizing internal files across a project and the Next.js ecosystem.
00275| - Sorting and grouping files in code editors.
00276| - Avoiding potential naming conflicts with future Next.js file conventions.
00277| 
00278| > **Good to know**:
00279| >
00280| > - While not a framework convention, you might also consider marking files outside private folders as "private" using the same underscore pattern.
00281| > - You can create URL segments that start with an underscore by prefixing the folder name with `%5F` (the URL-encoded form of an underscore): `%5FfolderName`.
00282| > - If you don't use private folders, it would be helpful to know Next.js [special file conventions](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#routing-files) to prevent unexpected naming conflicts.
00283| 
00284| ### Route groups
00285| 
00286| Route groups can be created by wrapping a folder in parenthesis: `(folderName)`
00287| 
00288| This indicates the folder is for organizational purposes and should **not be included** in the route's URL path.
00289| 
00290| <Image
00291|   alt="An example folder structure using route groups"
00292|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-route-groups.png"
00293|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-route-groups.png"
00294|   width="1600"
00295|   height="849"
00296| />
00297| 
00298| Route groups are useful for:
00299| 
00300| - Organizing routes by site section, intent, or team. e.g. marketing pages, admin pages, etc.
00301| - Enabling nested layouts in the same route segment level:
00302|   - [Creating multiple nested layouts in the same segment, including multiple root layouts](#creating-multiple-root-layouts)
00303|   - [Adding a layout to a subset of routes in a common segment](#opting-specific-segments-into-a-layout)
00304| 
00305| ### `src` folder
00306| 
00307| Next.js supports storing application code (including `app`) inside an optional [`src` folder](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder). This separates application code from project configuration files which mostly live in the root of a project.
00308| 
00309| <Image
00310|   alt="An example folder structure with the `src` folder"
00311|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-src-directory.png"
00312|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-src-directory.png"
00313|   width="1600"
00314|   height="687"
00315| />
00316| 
00317| ## Examples
00318| 
00319| The following section lists a very high-level overview of common strategies. The simplest takeaway is to choose a strategy that works for you and your team and be consistent across the project.
00320| 
00321| > **Good to know**: In our examples below, we're using `components` and `lib` folders as generalized placeholders, their naming has no special framework significance and your projects might use other folders like `ui`, `utils`, `hooks`, `styles`, etc.
00322| 
00323| ### Store project files outside of `app`
00324| 
00325| This strategy stores all application code in shared folders in the **root of your project** and keeps the `app` directory purely for routing purposes.
00326| 
00327| <Image
00328|   alt="An example folder structure with project files outside of app"
00329|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-project-root.png"
00330|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-project-root.png"
00331|   width="1600"
00332|   height="849"
00333| />
00334| 
00335| ### Store project files in top-level folders inside of `app`
00336| 
00337| This strategy stores all application code in shared folders in the **root of the `app` directory**.
00338| 
00339| <Image
00340|   alt="An example folder structure with project files inside app"
00341|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-app-root.png"
00342|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-app-root.png"
00343|   width="1600"
00344|   height="849"
00345| />
00346| 
00347| ### Split project files by feature or route
00348| 
00349| This strategy stores globally shared application code in the root `app` directory and **splits** more specific application code into the route segments that use them.
00350| 
00351| <Image
00352|   alt="An example folder structure with project files split by feature or route"
00353|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-app-root-split.png"
00354|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-app-root-split.png"
00355|   width="1600"
00356|   height="1011"
00357| />
00358| 
00359| ### Organize routes without affecting the URL path
00360| 
00361| To organize routes without affecting the URL, create a group to keep related routes together. The folders in parenthesis will be omitted from the URL (e.g. `(marketing)` or `(shop)`).
00362| 
00363| <Image
00364|   alt="Organizing Routes with Route Groups"
00365|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-organisation.png"
00366|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-organisation.png"
00367|   width="1600"
00368|   height="930"
00369| />
00370| 
00371| Even though routes inside `(marketing)` and `(shop)` share the same URL hierarchy, you can create a different layout for each group by adding a `layout.js` file inside their folders.
00372| 
00373| <Image
00374|   alt="Route Groups with Multiple Layouts"
00375|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-multiple-layouts.png"
00376|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-multiple-layouts.png"
00377|   width="1600"
00378|   height="768"
00379| />
00380| 
00381| ### Opting specific segments into a layout
00382| 
00383| To opt specific routes into a layout, create a new route group (e.g. `(shop)`) and move the routes that share the same layout into the group (e.g. `account` and `cart`). The routes outside of the group will not share the layout (e.g. `checkout`).
00384| 
00385| <Image
00386|   alt="Route Groups with Opt-in Layouts"
00387|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-opt-in-layouts.png"
00388|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-opt-in-layouts.png"
00389|   width="1600"
00390|   height="930"
00391| />
00392| 
00393| ### Opting for loading skeletons on a specific route
00394| 
00395| To apply a [loading skeleton](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) via a `loading.js` file to a specific route, create a new route group (e.g., `/(overview)`) and then move your `loading.tsx` inside that route group.
00396| 
00397| <Image
00398|   alt="Folder structure showing a loading.tsx and a page.tsx inside the route group"
00399|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-loading.png"
00400|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-loading.png"
00401|   width="1600"
00402|   height="444"
00403| />
00404| 
00405| Now, the `loading.tsx` file will only apply to your dashboard → overview page instead of all your dashboard pages without affecting the URL path structure.
00406| 
00407| ### Creating multiple root layouts
00408| 
00409| To create multiple [root layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout), remove the top-level `layout.js` file, and add a `layout.js` file inside each route group. This is useful for partitioning an application into sections that have a completely different UI or experience. The `<html>` and `<body>` tags need to be added to each root layout.
00410| 
00411| <Image
00412|   alt="Route Groups with Multiple Root Layouts"
00413|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-multiple-root-layouts.png"
00414|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-multiple-root-layouts.png"
00415|   width="1600"
00416|   height="687"
00417| />
00418| 
00419| In the example above, both `(marketing)` and `(shop)` have their own root layout.
00420| 
00421| </AppOnly>
00422| 

(End of file - total 422 lines)

00005| ---
00006| 
00007| This page provides an overview of **all** the folder and file conventions in Next.js, and recommendations for organizing your project.
00008| 
00009| ## Folder and file conventions
00010| 
00011| ### Top-level folders
00012| 
00013| Top-level folders are used to organize your application's code and static assets.
00014| 
00015| <Image
00016|   alt="Route segments to path segments"
00017|   srcLight="/docs/light/top-level-folders.png"
00018|   srcDark="/docs/dark/top-level-folders.png"
00019|   width="1600"
00020|   height="525"
00021| />
00022| 
00023| |                                                                    |                                    |
00024| | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
00025| | [`app`](/docs/app)                                                 | App Router                         |
00026| | [`pages`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing)           | Pages Router                       |
00027| | [`public`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/public-folder) | Static assets to be served         |
00028| | [`src`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder)       | Optional application source folder |
00029| 
00030| ### Top-level files
00031| 
00032| Top-level files are used to configure your application, manage dependencies, run proxy, integrate monitoring tools, and define environment variables.
00033| 
00034| |                                                                              |                                                                                    |
00035| | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00036| | **Next.js**                                                                  |                                                                                    |
00037| | [`next.config.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js)            | Configuration file for Next.js                                                     |
00038| | [`package.json`](/docs/app/getting-started/installation#manual-installation) | Project dependencies and scripts                                                   |
00039| | [`instrumentation.ts`](/docs/app/guides/instrumentation)                     | OpenTelemetry and Instrumentation file                                             |
00040| | [`proxy.ts`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy)                 | Next.js request proxy                                                              |
00041| | [`.env`](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables)                             | Environment variables (should not be tracked by version control)                   |
00042| | [`.env.local`](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables)                       | Local environment variables (should not be tracked by version control)             |
00043| | [`.env.production`](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables)                  | Production environment variables (should not be tracked by version control)        |
00044| | [`.env.development`](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables)                 | Development environment variables (should not be tracked by version control)       |
00045| | [`eslint.config.mjs`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint)                 | Configuration file for ESLint                                                      |
00046| | `.gitignore`                                                                 | Git files and folders to ignore                                                    |
00047| | [`next-env.d.ts`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/typescript#next-envdts)     | TypeScript declaration file for Next.js (should not be tracked by version control) |
00048| | `tsconfig.json`                                                              | Configuration file for TypeScript                                                  |
00049| | `jsconfig.json`                                                              | Configuration file for JavaScript                                                  |
00050| 
00051| <AppOnly>
00052| 
00053| ### Routing Files
00054| 
00055| Add `page` to expose a route, `layout` for shared UI such as header, nav, or footer, `loading` for skeletons, `error` for error boundaries, and `route` for APIs.
00056| 
00057| |                                                                               |                     |                              |
00058| | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------- |
00059| | [`layout`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout)                   | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Layout                       |
00060| | [`page`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page)                       | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Page                         |
00061| | [`loading`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading)                 | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Loading UI                   |
00062| | [`not-found`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found)             | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Not found UI                 |
00063| | [`error`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error)                     | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Error UI                     |
00064| | [`global-error`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error#global-error) | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Global error UI              |
00065| | [`route`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route)                     | `.js` `.ts`         | API endpoint                 |
00066| | [`template`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/template)               | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Re-rendered layout           |
00067| | [`default`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default)                 | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Parallel route fallback page |
00068| 
00069| ### Nested routes
00070| 
00071| Folders define URL segments. Nesting folders nests segments. Layouts at any level wrap their child segments. A route becomes public when a `page` or `route` file exists.
00072| 
00073| | Path                        | URL pattern     | Notes                         |
00074| | --------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------- |
00075| | `app/layout.tsx`            | —               | Root layout wraps all routes  |
00076| | `app/blog/layout.tsx`       | —               | Wraps `/blog` and descendants |
00077| | `app/page.tsx`              | `/`             | Public route                  |
00078| | `app/blog/page.tsx`         | `/blog`         | Public route                  |
00079| | `app/blog/authors/page.tsx` | `/blog/authors` | Public route                  |
00080| 
00081| ### Dynamic routes
00082| 
00083| Parameterize segments with square brackets. Use `[segment]` for a single param, `[...segment]` for catch‑all, and `[[...segment]]` for optional catch‑all. Access values via the [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) prop.
00084| 
00085| | Path                            | URL pattern                                                          |
00086| | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00087| | `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`      | `/blog/my-first-post`                                                |
00088| | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.tsx`   | `/shop/clothing`, `/shop/clothing/shirts`                            |
00089| | `app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx` | `/docs`, `/docs/layouts-and-pages`, `/docs/api-reference/use-router` |
00090| 
00091| ### Route groups and private folders
00092| 
00093| Organize code without changing URLs with route groups [`(group)`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-groups#convention), and colocate non-routable files with private folders [`_folder`](#private-folders).
00094| 
00095| | Path                            | URL pattern | Notes                                     |
00096| | ------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
00097| | `app/(marketing)/page.tsx`      | `/`         | Group omitted from URL                    |
00098| | `app/(shop)/cart/page.tsx`      | `/cart`     | Share layouts within `(shop)`             |
00099| | `app/blog/_components/Post.tsx` | —           | Not routable; safe place for UI utilities |
00100| | `app/blog/_lib/data.ts`         | —           | Not routable; safe place for utils        |
00101| 
00102| ### Parallel and Intercepted Routes
00103| 
00104| These features fit specific UI patterns, such as slot-based layouts or modal routing.
00105| 
00106| Use `@slot` for named slots rendered by a parent layout. Use intercept patterns to render another route inside the current layout without changing the URL, for example, to show a details view as a modal over a list.
00107| 
00108| | Pattern (docs)                                                                              | Meaning              | Typical use case                         |
00109| | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
00110| | [`@folder`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes#slots)                 | Named slot           | Sidebar + main content                   |
00111| | [`(.)folder`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes#convention)      | Intercept same level | Preview sibling route in a modal         |
00112| | [`(..)folder`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes#convention)     | Intercept parent     | Open a child of the parent as an overlay |
00113| | [`(..)(..)folder`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes#convention) | Intercept two levels | Deeply nested overlay                    |
00114| | [`(...)folder`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes#convention)    | Intercept from root  | Show arbitrary route in current view     |
00115| 
00116| ### Metadata file conventions
00117| 
00118| #### App icons
00119| 
00120| |                                                                                                                 |                                     |                          |
00121| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------ |

00187| 
00188| ## Organizing your project
00189| 
00190| Next.js is **unopinionated** about how you organize and colocate your project files. But it does provide several features to help you organize your project.
00191| 
00192| ### Component hierarchy
00193| 
00194| The components defined in special files are rendered in a specific hierarchy:
00195| 
00196| - `layout.js`
00197| - `template.js`
00198| - `error.js` (React error boundary)
00199| - `loading.js` (React suspense boundary)
00200| - `not-found.js` (React error boundary for "not found" UI)
00201| - `page.js` or nested `layout.js`
00202| 
00203| <Image
00204|   alt="Component Hierarchy for File Conventions"
00205|   srcLight="/docs/light/file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00206|   srcDark="/docs/dark/file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00207|   width="1600"
00208|   height="643"
00209| />
00210| 
00211| The components are rendered recursively in nested routes, meaning the components of a route segment will be nested **inside** the components of its parent segment.
00212| 
00213| <Image
00214|   alt="Nested File Conventions Component Hierarchy"
00215|   srcLight="/docs/light/nested-file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00216|   srcDark="/docs/dark/nested-file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00217|   width="1600"
00218|   height="863"
00219| />
00220| 
00221| ### Colocation
00222| 
00223| In the `app` directory, nested folders define route structure. Each folder represents a route segment that is mapped to a corresponding segment in a URL path.
00224| 
00225| However, even though route structure is defined through folders, a route is **not publicly accessible** until a `page.js` or `route.js` file is added to a route segment.
00226| 
00227| <Image
00228|   alt="A diagram showing how a route is not publicly accessible until a page.js or route.js file is added to a route segment."
00229|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-not-routable.png"
00230|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-not-routable.png"
00231|   width="1600"
00232|   height="444"
00233| />
00234| 
00235| And, even when a route is made publicly accessible, only the **content returned** by `page.js` or `route.js` is sent to the client.
00236| 
00237| <Image
00238|   alt="A diagram showing how page.js and route.js files make routes publicly accessible."
00239|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-routable.png"
00240|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-routable.png"
00241|   width="1600"
00242|   height="687"
00243| />
00244| 
00245| This means that **project files** can be **safely colocated** inside route segments in the `app` directory without accidentally being routable.
00246| 
00247| <Image
00248|   alt="A diagram showing colocated project files are not routable even when a segment contains a page.js or route.js file."
00249|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-colocation.png"
00250|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-colocation.png"
00251|   width="1600"
00252|   height="1011"
00253| />
00254| 
00255| > **Good to know**: While you **can** colocate your project files in `app` you don't **have** to. If you prefer, you can [keep them outside the `app` directory](#store-project-files-outside-of-app).
00256| 
00257| ### Private folders
00258| 
00259| Private folders can be created by prefixing a folder with an underscore: `_folderName`
00260| 
00261| This indicates the folder is a private implementation detail and should not be considered by the routing system, thereby **opting the folder and all its subfolders** out of routing.
00262| 
00263| <Image
00264|   alt="An example folder structure using private folders"
00265|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-private-folders.png"
00266|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-private-folders.png"
00267|   width="1600"
00268|   height="849"
00269| />
00270| 
00271| Since files in the `app` directory can be [safely colocated by default](#colocation), private folders are not required for colocation. However, they can be useful for:
00272| 
00273| - Separating UI logic from routing logic.
00274| - Consistently organizing internal files across a project and the Next.js ecosystem.
00275| - Sorting and grouping files in code editors.
00276| - Avoiding potential naming conflicts with future Next.js file conventions.
00277| 
00278| > **Good to know**:
00279| >
00280| > - While not a framework convention, you might also consider marking files outside private folders as "private" using the same underscore pattern.
00281| > - You can create URL segments that start with an underscore by prefixing the folder name with `%5F` (the URL-encoded form of an underscore): `%5FfolderName`.
00282| > - If you don't use private folders, it would be helpful to know Next.js [special file conventions](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#routing-files) to prevent unexpected naming conflicts.
00283| 
00284| ### Route groups
00285| 
00286| Route groups can be created by wrapping a folder in parenthesis: `(folderName)`
00287| 
00288| This indicates the folder is for organizational purposes and should **not be included** in the route's URL path.
00289| 
00290| <Image
00291|   alt="An example folder structure using route groups"
00292|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-route-groups.png"
00293|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-route-groups.png"
00294|   width="1600"
00295|   height="849"
00296| />
00297| 
00298| Route groups are useful for:
00299| 
00300| - Organizing routes by site section, intent, or team. e.g. marketing pages, admin pages, etc.
00301| - Enabling nested layouts in the same route segment level:
00302|   - [Creating multiple nested layouts in the same segment, including multiple root layouts](#creating-multiple-root-layouts)
00303|   - [Adding a layout to a subset of routes in a common segment](#opting-specific-segments-into-a-layout)
00304| 
00305| ### `src` folder
00306| 
00307| Next.js supports storing application code (including `app`) inside an optional [`src` folder](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder). This separates application code from project configuration files which mostly live in the root of a project.
00308| 
00309| <Image
00310|   alt="An example folder structure with the `src` folder"
00311|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-src-directory.png"
00312|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-src-directory.png"
00313|   width="1600"
00314|   height="687"
00315| />
00316| 
00317| ## Examples
00318| 
00319| The following section lists a very high-level overview of common strategies. The simplest takeaway is to choose a strategy that works for you and your team and be consistent across the project.
00320| 
00321| > **Good to know**: In our examples below, we're using `components` and `lib` folders as generalized placeholders, their naming has no special framework significance and your projects might use other folders like `ui`, `utils`, `hooks`, `styles`, etc.
00322| 
00323| ### Store project files outside of `app`
00324| 
00325| This strategy stores all application code in shared folders in the **root of your project** and keeps the `app` directory purely for routing purposes.
00326| 
00327| <Image
00328|   alt="An example folder structure with project files outside of app"
00329|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-project-root.png"
00330|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-project-root.png"
00331|   width="1600"
00332|   height="849"
00333| />
00334| 
00335| ### Store project files in top-level folders inside of `app`
00336| 
00337| This strategy stores all application code in shared folders in the **root of the `app` directory**.
00338| 
00339| <Image
00340|   alt="An example folder structure with project files inside app"
00341|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-app-root.png"
00342|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-app-root.png"
00343|   width="1600"
00344|   height="849"
00345| />
00346| 
00347| ### Split project files by feature or route
00348| 
00349| This strategy stores globally shared application code in the root `app` directory and **splits** more specific application code into the route segments that use them.
00350| 
00351| <Image
00352|   alt="An example folder structure with project files split by feature or route"
00353|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-app-root-split.png"
00354|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-app-root-split.png"
00355|   width="1600"
00356|   height="1011"
00357| />
00358| 
00359| ### Organize routes without affecting the URL path
00360| 
00361| To organize routes without affecting the URL, create a group to keep related routes together. The folders in parenthesis will be omitted from the URL (e.g. `(marketing)` or `(shop)`).
00362| 
00363| <Image
00364|   alt="Organizing Routes with Route Groups"
00365|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-organisation.png"
00366|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-organisation.png"
00367|   width="1600"
00368|   height="930"
00369| />
00370| 
00371| Even though routes inside `(marketing)` and `(shop)` share the same URL hierarchy, you can create a different layout for each group by adding a `layout.js` file inside their folders.
00372| 
00373| <Image
00374|   alt="Route Groups with Multiple Layouts"
00375|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-multiple-layouts.png"
00376|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-multiple-layouts.png"
00377|   width="1600"
00378|   height="768"
00379| />
00380| 
00381| ### Opting specific segments into a layout
00382| 
00383| To opt specific routes into a layout, create a new route group (e.g. `(shop)`) and move the routes that share the same layout into the group (e.g. `account` and `cart`). The routes outside of the group will not share the layout (e.g. `checkout`).
00384| 
00385| <Image
00386|   alt="Route Groups with Opt-in Layouts"
00387|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-opt-in-layouts.png"
00388|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-opt-in-layouts.png"
00389|   width="1600"
00390|   height="930"
00391| />
00392| 
00393| ### Opting for loading skeletons on a specific route
00394| 
00395| To apply a [loading skeleton](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) via a `loading.js` file to a specific route, create a new route group (e.g., `/(overview)`) and then move your `loading.tsx` inside that route group.
00396| 
00397| <Image
00398|   alt="Folder structure showing a loading.tsx and a page.tsx inside the route group"
00399|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-loading.png"
00400|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-loading.png"
00401|   width="1600"
00402|   height="444"
00403| />
00404| 
00405| Now, the `loading.tsx` file will only apply to your dashboard → overview page instead of all your dashboard pages without affecting the URL path structure.
00406| 
00407| ### Creating multiple root layouts
00408| 
00409| To create multiple [root layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout), remove the top-level `layout.js` file, and add a `layout.js` file inside each route group. This is useful for partitioning an application into sections that have a completely different UI or experience. The `<html>` and `<body>` tags need to be added to each root layout.
00410| 
00411| <Image
00412|   alt="Route Groups with Multiple Root Layouts"
00413|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-multiple-root-layouts.png"
00414|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-multiple-root-layouts.png"
00415|   width="1600"
00416|   height="687"
00417| />
00418| 
00419| In the example above, both `(marketing)` and `(shop)` have their own root layout.
00420| 
00421| </AppOnly>
00422|

00006| 
00007| This page provides an overview of **all** the folder and file conventions in Next.js, and recommendations for organizing your project.
00008| 
00009| ## Folder and file conventions
00010| 
00011| ### Top-level folders
00012| 
00013| Top-level folders are used to organize your application's code and static assets.
00014| 
00015| <Image
00016|   alt="Route segments to path segments"
00017|   srcLight="/docs/light/top-level-folders.png"
00018|   srcDark="/docs/dark/top-level-folders.png"

00020|   height="525"
00021| />
00022| 
00023| |                                                                    |                                    |
00024| | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
00025| | [`app`](/docs/app)                                                 | App Router                         |
00026| | [`pages`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing)           | Pages Router                       |
00027| | [`public`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/public-folder) | Static assets to be served         |
00028| | [`src`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder)       | Optional application source folder |
00029| 
00030| ### Top-level files
00031| 
00032| Top-level files are used to configure your application, manage dependencies, run proxy, integrate monitoring tools, and define environment variables.
00033| 
00034| |                                                                              |                                                                                    |
00035| | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00036| | **Next.js**                                                                  |                                                                                    |
00037| | [`next.config.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js)            | Configuration file for Next.js                                                     |
00038| | [`package.json`](/docs/app/getting-started/installation#manual-installation) | Project dependencies and scripts                                                   |
00039| | [`instrumentation.ts`](/docs/app/guides/instrumentation)                     | OpenTelemetry and Instrumentation file                                             |
00040| | [`proxy.ts`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy)                 | Next.js request proxy                                                              |
00041| | [`.env`](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables)                             | Environment variables (should not be tracked by version control)                   |
00042| | [`.env.local`](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables)                       | Local environment variables (should not be tracked by version control)             |
00043| | [`.env.production`](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables)                  | Production environment variables (should not be tracked by version control)        |
00044| | [`.env.development`](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables)                 | Development environment variables (should not be tracked by version control)       |
00045| | [`eslint.config.mjs`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint)                 | Configuration file for ESLint                                                      |
00046| | `.gitignore`                                                                 | Git files and folders to ignore                                                    |
00047| | [`next-env.d.ts`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/typescript#next-envdts)     | TypeScript declaration file for Next.js (should not be tracked by version control) |
00048| | `tsconfig.json`                                                              | Configuration file for TypeScript                                                  |
00049| | `jsconfig.json`                                                              | Configuration file for JavaScript                                                  |
00050| 
00051| <AppOnly>
00052| 
00053| ### Routing Files
00054| 
00055| Add `page` to expose a route, `layout` for shared UI such as header, nav, or footer, `loading` for skeletons, `error` for error boundaries, and `route` for APIs.
00056| 
00057| |                                                                               |                     |                              |
00058| | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------- |
00059| | [`layout`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout)                   | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Layout                       |
00060| | [`page`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page)                       | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Page                         |
00061| | [`loading`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading)                 | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Loading UI                   |
00062| | [`not-found`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found)             | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Not found UI                 |
00063| | [`error`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error)                     | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Error UI                     |
00064| | [`global-error`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error#global-error) | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Global error UI              |
00065| | [`route`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route)                     | `.js` `.ts`         | API endpoint                 |
00066| | [`template`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/template)               | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Re-rendered layout           |
00067| | [`default`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default)                 | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Parallel route fallback page |
00068| 
00069| ### Nested routes
00070| 
00071| Folders define URL segments. Nesting folders nests segments. Layouts at any level wrap their child segments. A route becomes public when a `page` or `route` file exists.
00072| 
00073| | Path                        | URL pattern     | Notes                         |
00074| | --------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------- |
00075| | `app/layout.tsx`            | —               | Root layout wraps all routes  |
00076| | `app/blog/layout.tsx`       | —               | Wraps `/blog` and descendants |
00077| | `app/page.tsx`              | `/`             | Public route                  |
00078| | `app/blog/page.tsx`         | `/blog`         | Public route                  |
00079| | `app/blog/authors/page.tsx` | `/blog/authors` | Public route                  |
00080| 
00081| ### Dynamic routes
00082| 
00083| Parameterize segments with square brackets. Use `[segment]` for a single param, `[...segment]` for catch‑all, and `[[...segment]]` for optional catch‑all. Access values via the [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) prop.
00084| 
00085| | Path                            | URL pattern                                                          |
00086| | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00087| | `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`      | `/blog/my-first-post`                                                |
00088| | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.tsx`   | `/shop/clothing`, `/shop/clothing/shirts`                            |
00089| | `app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx` | `/docs`, `/docs/layouts-and-pages`, `/docs/api-reference/use-router` |
00090| 
00091| ### Route groups and private folders
00092| 
00093| Organize code without changing URLs with route groups [`(group)`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-groups#convention), and colocate non-routable files with private folders [`_folder`](#private-folders).
00094| 
00095| | Path                            | URL pattern | Notes                                     |
00096| | ------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
00097| | `app/(marketing)/page.tsx`      | `/`         | Group omitted from URL                    |
00098| | `app/(shop)/cart/page.tsx`      | `/cart`     | Share layouts within `(shop)`             |
00099| | `app/blog/_components/Post.tsx` | —           | Not routable; safe place for UI utilities |
00100| | `app/blog/_lib/data.ts`         | —           | Not routable; safe place for utils        |
00101| 
00102| ### Parallel and Intercepted Routes
00103| 
00104| These features fit specific UI patterns, such as slot-based layouts or modal routing.
00105| 
00106| Use `@slot` for named slots rendered by a parent layout. Use intercept patterns to render another route inside the current layout without changing the URL, for example, to show a details view as a modal over a list.
00107|

00160| ### Routes
00161| 
00162| |                                                                                                |                     |             |
00163| | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------- |
00164| | **Folder convention**                                                                          |                     |             |
00165| | [`index`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts#index-routes)        | `.js` `.jsx` `.tsx` | Home page   |

00186| <AppOnly>
00187| 
00188| ## Organizing your project
00189| 
00190| Next.js is **unopinionated** about how you organize and colocate your project files. But it does provide several features to help you organize your project.
00191| 
00192| ### Component hierarchy
00193| 
00194| The components defined in special files are rendered in a specific hierarchy:
00195| 
00196| - `layout.js`
00197| - `template.js`
00198| - `error.js` (React error boundary)
00199| - `loading.js` (React suspense boundary)
00200| - `not-found.js` (React error boundary for "not found" UI)
00201| - `page.js` or nested `layout.js`
00202| 
00203| <Image
00204|   alt="Component Hierarchy for File Conventions"
00205|   srcLight="/docs/light/file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00206|   srcDark="/docs/dark/file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00207|   width="1600"
00208|   height="643"
00209| />
00210| 
00211| The components are rendered recursively in nested routes, meaning the components of a route segment will be nested **inside** the components of its parent segment.
00212| 
00213| <Image
00214|   alt="Nested File Conventions Component Hierarchy"
00215|   srcLight="/docs/light/nested-file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00216|   srcDark="/docs/dark/nested-file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png"
00217|   width="1600"
00218|   height="863"
00219| />
00220| 
00221| ### Colocation
00222| 
00223| In the `app` directory, nested folders define route structure. Each folder represents a route segment that is mapped to a corresponding segment in a URL path.
00224| 
00225| However, even though route structure is defined through folders, a route is **not publicly accessible** until a `page.js` or `route.js` file is added to a route segment.
00226| 
00227| <Image
00228|   alt="A diagram showing how a route is not publicly accessible until a page.js or route.js file is added to a route segment."
00229|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-not-routable.png"
00230|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-not-routable.png"
00231|   width="1600"
00232|   height="444"
00233| />
00234| 
00235| And, even when a route is made publicly accessible, only the **content returned** by `page.js` or `route.js` is sent to the client.
00236| 
00237| <Image
00238|   alt="A diagram showing how page.js and route.js files make routes publicly accessible."
00239|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-routable.png"
00240|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-routable.png"
00241|   width="1600"
00242|   height="687"
00243| />
00244| 
00245| This means that **project files** can be **safely colocated** inside route segments in the `app` directory without accidentally being routable.
00246| 
00247| <Image
00248|   alt="A diagram showing colocated project files are not routable even when a segment contains a page.js or route.js file."
00249|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-colocation.png"
00250|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-colocation.png"
00251|   width="1600"
00252|   height="1011"
00253| />
00254| 
00255| > **Good to know**: While you **can** colocate your project files in `app` you don't **have** to. If you prefer, you can [keep them outside the `app` directory](#store-project-files-outside-of-app).
00256| 
00257| ### Private folders
00258| 
00259| Private folders can be created by prefixing a folder with an underscore: `_folderName`
00260| 
00261| This indicates the folder is a private implementation detail and should not be considered by the routing system, thereby **opting the folder and all its subfolders** out of routing.
00262| 
00263| <Image
00264|   alt="An example folder structure using private folders"
00265|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-private-folders.png"
00266|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-private-folders.png"
00267|   width="1600"
00268|   height="849"
00269| />
00270| 
00271| Since files in the `app` directory can be [safely colocated by default](#colocation), private folders are not required for colocation. However, they can be useful for:
00272| 
00273| - Separating UI logic from routing logic.
00274| - Consistently organizing internal files across a project and the Next.js ecosystem.
00275| - Sorting and grouping files in code editors.
00276| - Avoiding potential naming conflicts with future Next.js file conventions.
00277| 
00278| > **Good to know**:
00279| >
00280| > - While not a framework convention, you might also consider marking files outside private folders as "private" using the same underscore pattern.
00281| > - You can create URL segments that start with an underscore by prefixing the folder name with `%5F` (the URL-encoded form of an underscore): `%5FfolderName`.
00282| > - If you don't use private folders, it would be helpful to know Next.js [special file conventions](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#routing-files) to prevent unexpected naming conflicts.
00283| 
00284| ### Route groups
00285| 
00286| Route groups can be created by wrapping a folder in parenthesis: `(folderName)`
00287| 
00288| This indicates the folder is for organizational purposes and should **not be included** in the route's URL path.
00289| 
00290| <Image
00291|   alt="An example folder structure using route groups"
00292|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-route-groups.png"
00293|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-route-groups.png"
00294|   width="1600"
00295|   height="849"
00296| />
00297| 
00298| Route groups are useful for:
00299| 
00300| - Organizing routes by site section, intent, or team. e.g. marketing pages, admin pages, etc.
00301| - Enabling nested layouts in the same route segment level:
00302|   - [Creating multiple nested layouts in the same segment, including multiple root layouts](#creating-multiple-root-layouts)
00303|   - [Adding a layout to a subset of routes in a common segment](#opting-specific-segments-into-a-layout)
00304| 
00305| ### `src` folder
00306| 
00307| Next.js supports storing application code (including `app`) inside an optional [`src` folder](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder). This separates application code from project configuration files which mostly live in the root of a project.
00308| 
00309| <Image
00310|   alt="An example folder structure with the `src` folder"
00311|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-src-directory.png"
00312|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-src-directory.png"
00313|   width="1600"
00314|   height="687"
00315| />
00316| 
00317| ## Examples
00318| 
00319| The following section lists a very high-level overview of common strategies. The simplest takeaway is to choose a strategy that works for you and your team and be consistent across the project.
00320| 
00321| > **Good to know**: In our examples below, we're using `components` and `lib` folders as generalized placeholders, their naming has no special framework significance and your projects might use other folders like `ui`, `utils`, `hooks`, `styles`, etc.
00322| 
00323| ### Store project files outside of `app`
00324| 
00325| This strategy stores all application code in shared folders in the **root of your project** and keeps the `app` directory purely for routing purposes.
00326| 
00327| <Image
00328|   alt="An example folder structure with project files outside of app"
00329|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-project-root.png"
00330|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-project-root.png"
00331|   width="1600"
00332|   height="849"
00333| />
00334| 
00335| ### Store project files in top-level folders inside of `app`
00336| 
00337| This strategy stores all application code in shared folders in the **root of the `app` directory**.
00338| 
00339| <Image
00340|   alt="An example folder structure with project files inside app"
00341|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-app-root.png"
00342|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-app-root.png"
00343|   width="1600"
00344|   height="849"
00345| />
00346| 
00347| ### Split project files by feature or route
00348| 
00349| This strategy stores globally shared application code in the root `app` directory and **splits** more specific application code into the route segments that use them.
00350| 
00351| <Image
00352|   alt="An example folder structure with project files split by feature or route"
00353|   srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-app-root-split.png"
00354|   srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-app-root-split.png"
00355|   width="1600"
00356|   height="1011"
00357| />
00358| 
00359| ### Organize routes without affecting the URL path
00360| 
00361| To organize routes without affecting the URL, create a group to keep related routes together. The folders in parenthesis will be omitted from the URL (e.g. `(marketing)` or `(shop)`).
00362| 
00363| <Image
00364|   alt="Organizing Routes with Route Groups"
00365|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-organisation.png"
00366|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-organisation.png"
00367|   width="1600"
00368|   height="930"
00369| />
00370| 
00371| Even though routes inside `(marketing)` and `(shop)` share the same URL hierarchy, you can create a different layout for each group by adding a `layout.js` file inside their folders.
00372| 
00373| <Image
00374|   alt="Route Groups with Multiple Layouts"
00375|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-multiple-layouts.png"
00376|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-multiple-layouts.png"
00377|   width="1600"
00378|   height="768"
00379| />
00380| 
00381| ### Opting specific segments into a layout
00382| 
00383| To opt specific routes into a layout, create a new route group (e.g. `(shop)`) and move the routes that share the same layout into the group (e.g. `account` and `cart`). The routes outside of the group will not share the layout (e.g. `checkout`).
00384| 
00385| <Image
00386|   alt="Route Groups with Opt-in Layouts"
00387|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-opt-in-layouts.png"
00388|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-opt-in-layouts.png"
00389|   width="1600"
00390|   height="930"
00391| />
00392| 
00393| ### Opting for loading skeletons on a specific route
00394| 
00395| To apply a [loading skeleton](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) via a `loading.js` file to a specific route, create a new route group (e.g., `/(overview)`) and then move your `loading.tsx` inside that route group.
00396| 
00397| <Image
00398|   alt="Folder structure showing a loading.tsx and a page.tsx inside the route group"
00399|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-loading.png"
00400|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-loading.png"
00401|   width="1600"
00402|   height="444"
00403| />
00404| 
00405| Now, the `loading.tsx` file will only apply to your dashboard → overview page instead of all your dashboard pages without affecting the URL path structure.
00406| 
00407| ### Creating multiple root layouts
00408| 
00409| To create multiple [root layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout), remove the top-level `layout.js` file, and add a `layout.js` file inside each route group. This is useful for partitioning an application into sections that have a completely different UI or experience. The `<html>` and `<body>` tags need to be added to each root layout.
00410| 
00411| <Image
00412|   alt="Route Groups with Multiple Root Layouts"
00413|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-group-multiple-root-layouts.png"
00414|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-group-multiple-root-layouts.png"
00415|   width="1600"
00416|   height="687"
00417| />
00418| 
00419| In the example above, both `(marketing)` and `(shop)` have their own root layout.
00420| 
00421| </AppOnly>
00422|

In Next.js, routes are rendered on the server by default. This often means the client has to wait for a server response before a new route can be shown. Next.js comes with built-in [prefetching](#prefetching), [streaming](#streaming), and [client-side transitions](#client-side-transitions) ensuring navigation stays fast and responsive.

This guide explains how navigation works in Next.js and how you can optimize it for [dynamic routes](#dynamic-routes-without-loadingtsx) and [slow networks](#slow-networks).

## How navigation works

In Next.js, routes are rendered on the server by default. This often means the client has to wait for a server response before a new route can be shown. Next.js comes with built-in [prefetching](#prefetching), [streaming](#streaming), and [client-side transitions](#client-side-transitions) ensuring navigation stays fast and responsive.

This guide explains how navigation works in Next.js and how you can optimize it for [dynamic routes](#dynamic-routes-without-loadingtsx) and [slow networks](#slow-networks).

00002| title: How to upgrade to version 16
00003| nav_title: Version 16
00004| description: Upgrade your Next.js Application from Version 15 to 16.
00005| ---
00006| 
00007| {/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}
00008| 
00009| ## Upgrading from 15 to 16
00010| 
00011| ### Using AI Agents with Next.js DevTools MCP
00012| 
00013| If you're using an AI coding assistant that supports the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), you can use the **Next.js DevTools MCP** to automate the upgrade process and migration tasks.
00014| 
00015| #### Setup
00016| 
00017| Add the following configuration to your MCP client, for each coding agent you can read [this section](https://github.com/vercel/next-devtools-mcp#mcp-client-configuration) for configuration details.
00018| 
00019| **example:**
00020| 
00021| ```json filename=".mcp.json"
00022| {
00023|   "mcpServers": {
00024|     "next-devtools": {
00025|       "command": "npx",
00026|       "args": ["-y", "next-devtools-mcp@latest"]
00027|     }
00028|   }
00029| }
00030| ```
00031| 
00032| For more information, visit the [`next-devtools-mcp`](https://github.com/vercel/next-devtools-mcp) documentation to configure with your MCP client.
00033| 
00034| > **Note:** Using `next-devtools-mcp@latest` ensures that your MCP client will always use the latest version of the Next.js DevTools MCP server.
00035| 
00036| #### Example Prompts
00037| 
00038| Once configured, you can use natural language prompts to upgrade your Next.js app:
00039| 
00040| **To upgrade to Next.js 16:**
00041| 
00042| Connect to your coding agent and then prompt:
00043| 
00044| ```txt
00045| Next Devtools, help me upgrade my Next.js app to version 16
00046| ```
00047| 
00048| **To migrate to Cache Components (after upgrading to v16):**
00049| 
00050| Connect to your coding agent and then prompt:
00051| 
00052| ```txt
00053| Next Devtools, migrate my Next.js app to cache components
00054| ```
00055| 
00056| Learn more in the documentation [here](/docs/app/guides/mcp).
00057| 
00058| ### Using the Codemod
00059| 
00060| To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160):
00061| 
00062| ```bash package="pnpm"
00063| pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
00064| ```
00065| 
00066| ```bash package="npm"
00067| npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
00068| ```
00069| 
00070| ```bash package="yarn"
00071| yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
00072| ```
00073| 
00074| ```bash package="bun"
00075| bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
00076| ```
00077| 
00078| The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to:
00079| 
00080| - Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration
00081| - Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI
00082| - Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy`
00083| - Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs
00084| - Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts
00085| 
00086| If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions:
00087| 
00088| ```bash package="pnpm"
00089| pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
00090| ```
00091| 
00092| ```bash package="npm"
00093| npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
00094| ```
00095| 
00096| ```bash package="yarn"
00097| yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
00098| ```
00099| 
00100| ```bash package="bun"
00101| bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
00102| ```
00103| 
00104| If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions.
00105| 
00106| ## Node.js runtime and browser support
00107| 
00108| | Requirement   | Change / Details                                                   |
00109| | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00110| | Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported |
00111| | TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0`                                        |
00112| | Browsers      | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+                 |
00113| 
00114| ## Turbopack by default
00115| 
00116| Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build`
00117| 
00118| Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`.
00119| 
00120| ```json filename="package.json"
00121| {
00122|   "scripts": {
00123|     "dev": "next dev --turbopack",
00124|     "build": "next build --turbopack",
00125|     "start": "next start"
00126|   }
00127| }
00128| ```
00129| 
00130| This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts:
00131| 
00132| ```json filename="package.json"
00133| {
00134|   "scripts": {
00135|     "dev": "next dev",
00136|     "build": "next build",
00137|     "start": "next start"
00138|   }
00139| }
00140| ```
00141| 
00142| If your project has a [custom `webpack`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/webpack) configuration and you run `next build` (which now uses Turbopack by default), the build will **fail** to prevent misconfiguration issues.
00143| 
00144| You have a few different ways to address this:
00145| 
00146| - **Use Turbopack anyway:** Run with `next build --turbopack` to build using Turbopack and ignore your `webpack` config.
00147| - **Switch to Turbopack fully:** Migrate your `webpack` config to Turbopack-compatible options.
00148| - **Keep using Webpack:** Use the `--webpack` flag to opt out of Turbopack and build with Webpack.
00149| 
00150| > **Good to know**: If you see failing builds because a `webpack` configuration was found, but you don't define one yourself, it is likely that a plugin is adding a `webpack` option
00151| 
00152| ### Opting out of Turbopack
00153| 
00154| If you need to continue using Webpack, you can opt out with the `--webpack` flag. For example, to use Turbopack in development but Webpack for production builds:
00155|

00020| 
00021| ## The `viewport` object
00022| 
00023| To define the viewport options, export a `viewport` object from a `layout.jsx` or `page.jsx` file.
00024| 
00025| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
00026| import type { Viewport } from 'next'
00027|

00029|   themeColor: 'black',

00031| 
00032| export default function Page() {}

00037|   themeColor: 'black',
00038| }
00039| 
00040| export default function Page() {}
00041| ```
00042| 
00043| ## `generateViewport` function
00044| 
00045| `generateViewport` should return a [`Viewport` object](#viewport-fields) containing one or more viewport fields.
00046| 
00047| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
00048| export function generateViewport({ params }) {
00049|   return {
00050|     themeColor: '...',
00051|   }
00052| }
00053| ```

00062| }
00063| ```
